Modern.brandNameRationale: Cadence is the cyclist's word for pedaling rhythm. A real term, not a coined one. It sits in the head of every serious rider already. We name the brand after the thing every rider chases.

Modern.competitorLandscape: Rapha (rapha.cc) owns aspirational cycling clothing. Pas Normal Studios (pasnormalstudios.com) does it with more Copenhagen restraint. Specialized (specialized.com) is the performance hardware giant. We sit closest to Pas Normal in tone.
Modern.positioningStatement: Cycling gear for people who ride seriously and dress quietly.

Modern.positioningStatement: Road cycling kit for riders who care about the line, not the team kit.

Modern.tagline: If it doesn't show on the meter, it didn't happen.
Modern.brandNameRationale: Wattage is the single metric that defines modern road cycling. Naming the brand after the unit of work signals that every product decision is measured against it.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern cycling 2025+ is power-meter native. The opportunity is the data-aware roadie — kit, accessories, and small tools designed by people who actually own a Wahoo and look at numbers.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Wahoo Fitness (wahoofitness.com) is the data-platform peer. SRAM (sram.com) holds the wireless-shifting precedent. Hammerhead (hammerhead.io) sets the modern head-unit bar. We sit between Wahoo and SRAM as a kit-and-accessories brand.
Modern.positioningStatement: Cycling kit and gear for riders who train by the number.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Northerly is the wind. The long, cold, steady one that you ride into. It's also a direction. We chose a word that doesn't mention bicycles, because at this level, the brand isn't about the bike.
Luxury.story: Northerly began with three frames, hand built in a Brescia workshop, and a stubborn idea. The very best bicycle should not look like a bicycle from a magazine. It should look like a bicycle from a story your grandfather might have told.
Luxury.industrySummary: The top end of cycling has been chasing aerodynamics and grams. Bikes that look like spaceships. Riders who pay forty thousand euros for them. There's a smaller, quieter top tier asking for something different. Something heirloom.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Pegoretti (pegoretti.com) is the artisan reference. Cherubim (cherubim-jp.com) the Japanese counterpart. Mosaic (mosaiccycles.com) the American custom standard. We are in their company, with less typography and more silence.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A bicycle house for riders who want one bike for the next thirty years.

targetAudience.primary: 45 and up. Has had several bikes. Knows what a good frame feels like. Travels with the bike. Will pay for a frame the way they would pay for a piano.

Luxury.positioningStatement: Italian cycling kit for riders who care who stitched it.

Creative.brandNameRationale: SPOKE is a bike part. It's also the past tense of speak. The pun is the strategy. The brand has things to say, and the way it says them is by riding.
Creative.manifesto: We made Spoke because city cycling needed a brand that didn't take itself like a Tour de France team. We ride to the bar. We ride to the bagel shop. We ride because it's fun. Spoke is the brand for that rider.
Creative.industrySummary: Cycling brand world is full of capital P Performance brands. There are fewer brands speaking to the actual person who rides a bike in jeans to a party. Lots of room there.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Mash SF (mashsf.com) has the cult-cool. State Bicycle Co. (statebicycle.com) does playful but big. Brick Lane Bikes (bricklanebikes.co.uk) carries the London street culture. We are louder than all of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: A bike brand for people who ride for fun and dress like it.
